The Gujarat earthquake struck the Kutch district of western India on the morning of 26 January 2001, India's Republic Day. It measured 7.6 or 7.7 and killed about 20,000 people, injured some 166,000 and destroyed around 400,000 buildings.

The town of Bhuj and nearby Bhachau and Anjar were largely flattened. The shaking reached as far as Ahmedabad, where tall apartment blocks collapsed, and into Pakistan's Sindh. Kutch sits on old faults far from any plate edge, and it had been hit before, in 1819.

Rebuilding was large and fast, helped by money from abroad, and towns in Kutch were rebuilt with new roads and stricter building rules. Anger over relief helped bring a change of chief minister in Gujarat that October: Narendra Modi took office. The quake was the worst in India in fifty years, until the Indian Ocean tsunami of 2004. Other great South Asian quakes include the 1934 Bihar and Nepal earthquake and the Kashmir earthquake of 2005.
